title: Tenant Sabbatical & Isolation Circuit — PRD Draft
body:
Goal
Provide a low-friction, reversible mechanism for temporarily resting ("sabbatical") tenant reservations and routing their traffic through an isolation circuit so the platform can recover capacity, rebalance noisy neighbors, and execute prewarm/evacuation procedures without hard preemption.

Context and problem statement
- We get live incidents where a single tenant’s burst/traffic pattern causes noisy-neighbor effects on shared Dedicated pools. Hard preemption/eviction is disruptive for customers and support heavy.
- Customers want predictable latency SLOs for high-tier tenants but also need the ability to accept degraded performance during planned maintenance windows or when they knowingly want to free capacity for short periods (e.g., heavy offline training).
- Current options are heavy-handed: full eviction, manual reserve changes, or overprovisioning. We need a middle ground that is user-visible, reversible, observability-first, and operationally safe.

Proposal summary
Introduce two related features: (1) Tenant Sabbatical — a tenant-level, timeboxed suspension of reserved capacity that can be self-initiated or suggested by the platform, and (2) Isolation Circuit — a runtime routing and throttling layer that moves a sabbatical tenant (or any suspected noisy tenant) into a constrained, observable lane with controlled bursts and prewarm windows.

Key behaviors and UX
- Tenant Sabbatical: a customer (or operator) can place a reservation into sabbatical for X minutes/hours (default 2h). While on sabbatical:
  - Billing treatment: credit for unused reserved capacity (configurable) OR paused-billing option for enterprise.
  - Reservation is soft-reclaimed: other tenants may use excess capacity opportunistically.
  - Tenant continues to accept requests but is routed through the Isolation Circuit (see below) unless explicitly opted-out.

- Isolation Circuit: a controlled execution lane that provides:
  - Token-bucket rate shaping at tenant level (configurable buckets for soft-burst, sustained rate).
  - Latency SLO fences: admission control rejects requests that would violate configured SLO percentiles.
  - Structured prewarm window: small, scheduled warm-ups to populate KV caches for expected hot prefixes.
  - Graceful fallback paths: automatic routing to lower-cost model variants or hosted fallback if critical.

- Platform-initiated suggestions: platform may surface a "Recommend sabbatical" action when predictive signals show a tenant will cause high tail latency or overheating. Suggestions include an estimated impact and recommended duration.

Autoscaling & burst integration
- Sabbatical interacts with autoscaler as follows:
  - When a sabbatical is requested, the autoscaler marks the reservation as eligible for temporary decommit; predictive autoscaler may de-schedule warm-pool nodes for short windows.
  - Isolation Circuit enforces a soft burst cap: tenant can still burst up to X tokens/sec for Y seconds using a shared burst credit pool, then fall into sustained shape.
  - If overall pool utilization rises above a critical threshold, the circuit enacts a global soft-throttle that reduces all sabbatical and opportunistic bursts first.

Isolation controls and safety
- Isolation Circuit must be auditable: every decision (route, throttle, fallback) emits an event with tenant id, rule id, input signature, and pre/post metrics.
- Quarantine mode: operator can escalate a tenant from sabbatical -> quarantine, which places stronger constraints (hard throttles, model downgrade) for safety.
- Safety knobs for customers: allowlist of IPs/paths that bypass isolation (for admin hooks), SLA-protected routes that cannot be throttled below a floor.

Metrics and SLOs to track
- Tenant-level metrics: sabbatical_count, time_in_sabbatical, burst_credit_consumed, isolation_rejects, fallback_reroutes.
- Pool-level metrics: reclaimed_capacity_by_sabbatical, opportunistic_utilization, warm_pool_decommit_rate.
- Business metrics: expected_monthly_credit_given, customer_acceptance_rate_of_recommendations.

Operational runbook (initial sketch)
- When platform suggests sabbatical: support prints recommended script and Slack template to request customer consent.
- During a noisy neighbor incident: prefer moving noisy tenant to sabbatical+isolation circuit before preempting. Escalation path: support -> oncall SRE -> product ops.
- Rollback: immediate cancel sabbatical (rebind reservation) or phase out isolation rules.

Open design questions / TODOs
- Billing policy: credit percentage, opt-in paused billing, accounting changes needed.
- UX: how visible should platform recommendations be in Console vs. support ticket?
- Prewarm heuristics: deterministically pick prefixes to warm; how to avoid wasted GPU cycles?
- Burst economics: should burst credits be charged at premium rate to discourage abuse?
- Multi-reservation tenants: how to treat customers with several reservations across pools?

Implementation plan (milestones)
- M1 (6w): event model + API prototyping: sabbatical state, circuit flags, audit events. Console stub to toggle sabbatical.
- M2 (6w): runtime isolation circuit MVP: token bucket enforcement, simple prewarm hook, observable metrics.
- M3 (8w): autoscaler integration: markable reservations, warm-pool decommit, opportunistic reuse.
- M4 (4w): billing experiments + enterprise opt-in and docs.

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: customers misinterpret sabbatical as forced eviction -> mitigate via explicit consent flows and docs.
- Risk: prewarm wastes resources -> mitigate with conservative default prewarm sizes and telemetry.
- Risk: complexity in autoscaler interactions -> build feature-flagged rollout and chaos tests in staging.

Notes / references
- See linked artifacts for early simulation notebooks and the slack thread (#dedicated-ops) for recent incidents.
- Example Jira to track: ENG-4127 (simulation + autoscaler hooks).

Appendix: sample API snippets (draft)
- POST /api/v1/reservations/{id}/sabbatical { duration: "2h", mode: "soft" } -> returns sabbatical_id
- GET /api/v1/reservations/{id}/sabbatical/status -> { state: "active", burst_remaining: "12000" }

Quick wins / experiments to validate concept
- A/B test platform suggestion cards for 100 mid-tier tenants and measure acceptance/impact.
- Short runbook to use sabbatical + isolation in two recent incidents and measure MTTR improvement.

Authors and reviewers
- Drafted by: Aisha Patel (product)
- Reviewers: Marco Li (SRE), Priya Narayanan (serving runtime), Ethan Morales (billing)

End of draft — looking for feedback on billing model, autoscaler semantics, and customer UX wording.
